Re-checked on the embedded figure image (curve-to-potential assignment against the panel legend: green triangles = -0.65 V vs. RHE; plateau re-measured at about -19.5 mA/cm2), so the reading is kept. Recorded internal inconsistency of the source: the printed FE(HCOO-) = 31.6% and j(HCOO-) = -7.51 mA/cm2 of the same run (pp. 1, 6, 7) imply a total current density of about -23.8 mA/cm2, which matches the -0.65 V curve at early times (about -24 mA/cm2 at t = 200-400 s) rather than the end-of-run plateau; the printed FE/j pair thus appears to correspond to an earlier stage of the electrolysis than the plateau read here.

Each point read twice off the 600 dpi page image; the readings agreed within the stated uncertainty. Minus signs are lost in the PDF text layer and were taken from the page image. Re-checked on the embedded figure image (bars re-measured against the 0 and 40 % ticks): the readings stand. Recorded as read, the faradaic efficiencies sum to only about 68.5% at -0.55 V (37.7 + 4.9 + 25.9) and about 54.5% at -0.65 V (17.0 + 31.6 + 5.9), although the source states only H2, CO and HCOO- are detected on SnPS3 (p. 5) - a low FE closure, possible in a flow cell with unaccounted products or charge. The CO bar at -0.65 V (5.9%) also reads slightly higher than at -0.55 V (4.9%), whereas the source text states the FECO decreased according to the increased overpotential (p. 5); the figure is as read.
